companies.name: BuzzFeed
companies.what_they_did: It operated a digital news and media platform. It faced layoffs alongside other media sites.
companies.story: BuzzFeed is a digital media outlet that grew into a prominent online platform. The media industry faced challenges leading to job losses and restructuring. It continues to operate as a digital media company.
reasons: Navigated industry-wide ad revenue shifts towards social media platforms like Facebook and Google
Adapted its operations to survive changing consumer and advertiser habits
companies.one_line: Navigated advertising industry shifts driven by dominant social media platforms

risks_handled.how: Fought for survival against ad industry dominance by Facebook and Google through integration and adaptation

companies.name: HuffPost India
companies.what_they_did: It published digital news and investigative stories in India. It was shut down following new media ownership regulations.
companies.story: HuffPost India operated for six years, producing exceptional journalism under its editor-in-chief. It was forced to shut down after BuzzFeed acquired HuffPost from Verizon Media and new digital media ownership regulations were introduced in India.
reasons: Impacted by new government restrictions and regulations on digital media ownership in India
BuzzFeed decided to shut it down after acquiring HuffPost
companies.one_line: Faced new government restrictions and regulations on digital media ownership in India

causes.proof: HuffPost India was the first casualty of the Narendra Modi administration’s new restrictions on digital media ownership

companies.name: Quartz
companies.what_they_did: It operated a digital publication based in the U.S. It expanded its operations to India over the past decade.
companies.story: Quartz set up operations in India over the past decade as part of its international expansion. It navigated the changing digital media landscape and media regulations in the region. It remains active as a digital news publisher.
reasons: Expanded its digital publishing footprint internationally into growing internet markets
Navigated complex regulatory environments for digital media
companies.one_line: Expanded operations internationally while adapting to regional digital media changes

companies.name: Vice
companies.what_they_did: It produced digital media content. It established operations in India over the past decade.
companies.story: Vice expanded its digital media operations into India during the last decade alongside other U.S. publications. It continued operating as part of the evolving digital news ecosystem. It remains active in the media space.
reasons: Expanded internationally to capture emerging digital audience bases
Maintained operations amidst changing regulatory frameworks
companies.one_line: Expanded internationally into emerging digital markets

companies.name: The Wire
companies.what_they_did: It launched as a new digital venture in India. It publishes digital news and current affairs.
companies.story: The Wire launched as a new venture during a period of explosive internet growth in India. It established itself within the digital news landscape alongside other independent publishers. It continues to operate as an independent digital news outlet.
reasons: Capitalized on India's explosive internet and mobile data user growth
Leveraged digital independence free from traditional print limitations
companies.one_line: Capitalized on India's booming digital internet audience

companies.name: The News Minute
companies.what_they_did: It launched as a digital news venture in India. It covers digital news and regional events.
companies.story: The News Minute launched as a digital media venture during the expansion of internet usage in India. It operates within the digital newsroom ecosystem, catering to online audiences. It remains active as a digital news platform.
reasons: Reached mass digital audiences unconstrained by print limitations
Adapted to the changing digital news landscape in India
companies.one_line: Built a digital news platform catering to online Indian audiences

companies.name: Swarajya
companies.what_they_did: It launched as a digital media venture in India. It publishes digital commentary and news.
companies.story: Swarajya started as a new digital venture during a decade of rapid internet adoption in India. It established its presence online to reach readers across the country. It continues to operate as a digital publication.
reasons: Leveraged digital publishing to reach a wide online readership
Navigated the evolving digital media regulations in India
companies.one_line: Established a digital publication leveraging India's internet growth

companies.name: The Quint
companies.what_they_did: It launched as a digital news venture in India. It delivers digital news and multimedia stories.
companies.story: The Quint launched as part of the wave of new digital ventures during India's internet boom. It grew by catering to mass audiences through digital-first formats. It remains active as a digital news publisher.
reasons: Catered to mass audiences through digital-first storytelling
Adapted to shifting digital media industry conditions in India
companies.one_line: Built a digital-first news platform for online audiences in India

companies.name: Mediapart
companies.what_they_did: It operates as a digital native news media outlet providing investigative journalism and alternative revenue streams. It functions as an independent digital news organization in France.
companies.story: Mediapart was established in France as a digital native news outlet. It serves as a prominent example of discovering and testing new products and alternative revenue streams in digital journalism. It remains part of the digital news landscape.
reasons: It successfully established alternative revenue streams and innovative ways of organizing digital journalism.
It maintained a strong position as a digital-born news media outlet in Europe.
companies.one_line: It successfully operated as a digital native news media outlet with alternative revenue streams.

companies.name: De Correspondent
companies.what_they_did: It operates as a digital native news media outlet focused on ad-free, membership-funded journalism. It tests novel revenue streams and alternative ways of organizing digital journalism.
companies.story: De Correspondent started in the Netherlands as a digital native news organization. It emerged as an environment where new products and alternative revenue streams are discovered and tested. It continues to operate as an innovative journalism platform.
reasons: It pioneered alternative revenue streams and member-funded journalism models.
It focused on building an engaged audience through innovative digital organization.
companies.one_line: It maintained operations through a membership-funded and innovative digital news model.

companies.name: The Messenger
companies.what_they_did: It operated as a news site founded by Jimmy Finkelstein. It attempted a broad digital journalism model with high-profile staffing and large compensation packages.
companies.story: The Messenger launched as a news site backed by Jimmy Finkelstein. It faced criticism for a comical business plan and unsustainable spending. Ultimately, the site failed and shut down.
reasons: It suffered from a comical and unsustainable business plan.
It incurred excessive expenses, such as paying the editor in chief a very high salary.
companies.one_line: It failed due to a comical and unsustainable business plan with excessive expenses.

companies.name: NewsTilt
companies.what_they_did: It operated as a publishing platform designed to help journalists act as their own bosses. It provided tools for writers to publish their stories.
companies.story: NewsTilt started with the concept of supporting independent journalists as newspapers went out of business. It encountered problems with journalists not writing enough, distrusting Facebook, and lacking willingness to socially promote their work. The team ultimately decided to shut it down and return what was left.
reasons: Journalists were not writing enough and were unwilling to socially promote their work.
The creators realized it was not a good product for customers due to a lack of clear writing direction.
Alienation of people who disliked Facebook prevented the introduction of important features.
companies.one_line: It did not make a sufficiently good product for journalists and lacked proper product direction.

causes.proof: I realized that I didn’t believe that NewsTilt was a good product for either set of our customers.

companies.founder_words: All the problems the journalists faced, not writing enough, their distrust of Facebook, their unwillingness to socially promote their work, would not have been problems for a young journalist eager to make a name for himself.

companies.name: Vice News
companies.what_they_did: It operated as the news division of Vice Media focusing on ambitious investigative digital journalism. It produced groundbreaking content on global issues.
companies.story: Born out of a counter-culture magazine in Montreal, Vice Media evolved rapidly, and its news division, Vice News, became a formidable force in digital journalism. It eventually faced a brutal financial storm along with Vice Media Group filing for bankruptcy. This led to the inevitable closure of its news division.
reasons: It struggled to find a sustainable revenue model to keep pace with expensive content production.
It faced dwindling advertising revenues and relentless competition in a fragmented digital landscape.
companies.one_line: It struggled with a brutal financial storm and an unsustainable revenue model for expensive content production.

causes.proof: The announcement of Vice Media Group filing for bankruptcy and the subsequent, inevitable closure of its news division marked a significant moment

companies.name: Vice Media
companies.what_they_did: It operated as a media company born out of a counter-culture magazine in Montreal. It produced ambitious digital media content and investigative journalism.
companies.story: Vice Media evolved rapidly from a counter-culture magazine in Montreal into a major digital media company. Ultimately, it encountered a brutal financial storm and filed for bankruptcy, leading to the closure of its divisions like Vice News.
reasons: It struggled to find a sustainable revenue model that could keep pace with expensive content production.
It faced dwindling advertising revenues and intense competition from tech giants.
companies.one_line: It faced a brutal financial storm and filed for bankruptcy due to an unsustainable revenue model.

causes.proof: The announcement of Vice Media Group filing for bankruptcy and the subsequent, inevitable closure of its news division marked a significant moment

companies.name: RocaNews
companies.what_they_did: It operates as a digital news provider launched initially as an Instagram page. It delivers factual and non-partisan news using positive journalism and a gamified news app.
companies.story: RocaNews launched in August 2020, starting initially as an Instagram page. Within its first year, it achieved 1 million Instagram followers and secured over 200,000 newsletter subscribers. It continues to run by focusing on community-building and engaging, non-partisan content.
reasons: It focuses on delivering factual and non-partisan news instead of political narratives.
It employs positive journalism and builds a community around a gamified news app and newsletters.
companies.one_line: It differentiates itself through non-partisan positive journalism, newsletters, and a gamified news app.

companies.name: 404 Media
companies.what_they_did: It operates as a digital news startup focusing on technology, internet culture, and societal issues. It provides in-depth, critical reporting for target readers.
companies.story: 404 Media was launched in 2023 by former Vice Media journalists. It focuses on technology, internet culture, and the intersection of societal issues with emerging trends. It continues to operate as an independent media outlet.
reasons: It targets readers seeking in-depth, critical reporting in specialized areas.
It was founded by experienced journalists from Vice Media covering unique niches like internet culture.
companies.one_line: It provides specialized, in-depth reporting on technology and internet culture by former industry journalists.

companies.name: ThinkProgress
companies.what_they_did: Published progressive news and policy analysis. Operated as an editorially independent website backed by the Center for American Progress.
companies.story: ThinkProgress rose to prominence during the Bush administration and helped shape progressive voices as the Obama administration took over. Facing financial pressures and failing to find a new publisher or buyer, the site shut down suddenly and folded back into CAP's online presence.
reasons: Failed to acquire funding or find a new buyer.
Faced revenue losses and industry-wide shifts affecting media sites.
companies.one_line: Failed to acquire funding or find a new publisher to stay afloat.

causes.proof: Progressive media website ThinkProgress shut down this month after it failed to acquire funding.

companies.name: HuffPost
companies.what_they_did: Operated as a digital news and media site. Faced industry layoffs amid advertising revenue challenges.
companies.story: HuffPost experienced industry-wide job losses and revenue challenges as ad revenue shifted toward major social media platforms. The site continues to navigate the media industry landscape.
reasons: Faced industry layoffs and revenue losses.
Competed with dominant ad platforms like Facebook and Google.
companies.one_line: Faced media industry layoffs and revenue pressures.

companies.name: Artifact
companies.what_they_did: Created an AI-powered news application developed by Instagram's founders. Delivered personalized news content via an AI app.
companies.story: Created by the founders of Instagram, Artifact launched as an AI news app to deliver personalized news content. Ultimately, it failed to find its market and was discontinued.
reasons: Failed to find its market despite prominent founders.
Could not secure long-term user adoption.
companies.one_line: Failed to find its market and achieve sustainable success.

causes.proof: Artifact, the AI news app from Instagram's founders, failed to find its market.

companies.name: Rebel News
companies.what_they_did: Published independent news and commentary in Canada. Challenged government policies despite lacking official journalism tax license status.
companies.story: Founded by Ezra Levant, Rebel News operates as an independent media organization in Canada. It has faced scrutiny and legal battles regarding government accreditation and press access, but continues to publish independently.
reasons: Operated independently despite lacking government tax subsidies.
Fought legal battles to maintain press access and coverage rights.
companies.one_line: Maintained independent reporting operations despite government policy challenges.
companies.founder_words: It’s not yet illegal to do journalism without the license

companies.name: News Media Corporation
companies.what_they_did: Operated a conglomeration of small newspapers and shoppers across multiple states. Published local community news and print editions.
companies.story: News Media Corporation owned and operated numerous local newspapers and shoppers across various states. The company folded suddenly without warning, leading to a Chapter 7 bankruptcy declaration and the abrupt closure of all its publications.
reasons: Creditors took the company to court resulting in a Chapter 7 bankruptcy.
Sudden corporate closure with no warning given to employees.
companies.one_line: Declared Chapter 7 bankruptcy resulting in the sudden shutdown of all its publications.
companies.founder_words: We weren't given the opportunity to say goodbye

companies.name: Rappler
companies.what_they_did: Published investigative journalism and news coverage in the Philippines. Gained notoriety for reporting on government drug crackdowns.
companies.story: Co-founded by Nobel Peace laureate Maria Ressa, Rappler gained international attention for its investigative reporting. Although the Philippine government affirmed orders to revoke its certificates of incorporation, the organization has vowed to appeal and continues operations.
reasons: Fought government shutdown orders through legal appeals.
Maintained reporting operations despite regulatory and legal pressure.
companies.one_line: Fought government shutdown and revocation orders through ongoing legal appeals.
